summary: Initial-response stall for chat streaming after runtime kernel swap and model pin
summary_line_items: Customer reports repeated stalls of 3-6s before first token when using chat streaming since runtime kernel swap and model pining on 2026-03-09
description: Issue summary: Customer NovaLaw AI observed elevated initial latency (stall before first token) on streaming chat completions after we rolled a runtime kernel swap and they pinned dialog-7b-v2. Impact: customer-facing UX regression with user timeouts and increased support load. Environment: Prod us-east with Dedicated capacity. This ticket captures the triage, investigation, and short-term mitigations.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer pins model redwood/dialog-7b-v2 via API or Console.
2) Start a chat streaming session using the streaming endpoint with typical prompt sizes (context ~600 tokens).
3) Observe initial stall (no tokens emitted) for 3-6 seconds, then normal token emission.
4) Re-running on previous runtime node (rollback) removes the stall.
observed_behavior: Initial stall of 3-6s before first token for ~40% of streaming sessions; subsequent token throughput and latency within normal bounds.
expected_behavior: First token should stream within <500ms for typical pinned model and request size under Dedicated capacity SLA.

customer_impact: NovaLaw AI reported multiple production customer timeouts and one incident where a user-facing worker process retried requests resulting in duplicate logs. They requested urgent mitigation and root-cause confirmation.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 09:30 - Support triage: verified reproduced with customer test harness. Noted correlation with runtime kernel swap rolled 2026-03-09 01:45 UTC.
2026-03-10 10:15 - SRE attached perf traces: long kernel init (2.8s) for select kernel-v9 when model pinned to dialog-7b-v2-quant path.
2026-03-10 11:00 - Hypothesis A: kernel selection path now attempts a quantization fallback that triggers extra JIT or memory touch causing stall.
2026-03-10 12:20 - Hypothesis B: routing layer placed requests on a new node flavor optimized for throughput but with cold-start behavior for certain kernel shapes.
2026-03-10 14:05 - Reproduction: rolling nodes back to runtime revision r1.3.8 removed stall in 12/12 tests; forward revision r1.4.0 shows 9/12 stalls.

2026-03-11 08:30 - Kernel team found PR that changed eager-kernel-loading behavior (PR #2142) merged 2026-03-09. This toggles lazy->eager for some kernels but in certain memory layouts triggers page faults and stalls.
2026-03-11 12:45 - Confirmed that requesting non-quantized variant of the model reduces stalls; quantized path more affected.
2026-03-12 09:10 - Confirmed customer traffic pattern (many short chat sessions) increases probability of hitting cold kernel path on first token.
2026-03-12 11:00 - Risk assessment: rollback of PR #2142 on affected Dedicated pools is lowest-risk mitigation; longer-term fix to kernel prewarm logic under investigation.
comments: Support (Aisha Patel) 2026-03-10T09:35: We've reproduced with NovaLaw test harness. Attaching sample request IDs and perf traces. Requesting SRE assistance to look into kernel-level stalls.

SRE (Marco Rivera) 2026-03-10T10:05: Reviewing traces now. There's a clear 2.5-3s stall prior to first read from GPU in a subset of sessions. Assigning to kernel team.
Slack thread: #inc-ttfb (https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C023TTFB)

Kernel Eng (Priya Menon) 2026-03-11T08:40: We merged an eager-load change in PR #2142; checking if eager load could block due to page faults under certain VM flavors. Starting controlled rollback on one Dedicated pool.
Customer (NovaLaw Support - Oliver Chang) 2026-03-11T09:25: Appreciate the quick reproduction. Our users hit timeouts after 3s and we saw retries. Please advise workaround ASAP.
SRE (Marco Rivera) 2026-03-11T12:00: Short-term mitigation: we will roll back PR #2142 on affected Dedicated nodes in us-east. ETA 60m. Will monitor p95 first-token latency.
Support (Aisha Patel) 2026-03-11T13:15: NovaLaw confirmed reduced failed chats after rollback on their Dedicated pool. They request a postmortem and timeline for permanent fix.
root_cause: Eager kernel-loading change (PR #2142) introduced blocking kernel initialization on certain VM memory layouts, causing 2-4s stalls before the first token when requests hit a quantized kernel path for pinned models.
workaround: Rollback PR #2142 on affected Dedicated pools or force routing to runtime revision r1.3.8 for NovaLaw's reserved capacity. Alternatively, advise customer to use non-quantized model variant until fix is released.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-11 14:10 - Rolled back PR #2142 on Dedicated us-east pool serving NovaLaw. Observed p95 first-token latency drop from 4.5s -> 380ms over next 30 minutes. Customer confirmed recovery. Kernel team preparing non-blocking eager-load patch for next runtime patch release.
postmortem_actions: Action 1: Kernel team to implement non-blocking prewarm for eager-kernel-load (owner: Priya Menon) - target patch 2026-03-18
Action 2: Add canary testing for first-token latency on runtime kernel changes (owner: SRE) - due 2026-03-20
Action 3: Update rollout runbook to include rollback path and monitoring alert thresholds (owner: Ops) - due 2026-03-15
